   Probs
      Present at encounter:  Lorna Baker OT, Roy and Jean.
      Physical health:  S/ I saw Roy and his wife in their home at 10.30.  I introduced myself and explained my role.  Consent obtained to OT input.

I spent time talking with Roy and Jean regarding the set up at home and how Roy has been managing.  Roy and Jean live in their own bungalow where they have lived for over 30 years.  They have a son who lives in Loughborough and a daughter who lives in Blaby.  Roy reported that he is independently mobile inside the bungalow.  He reported that he uses a stick outdoors but the distance he is able to mobilise outdoors is limited due to breathlessness and fatigue.  He reported that he also has a mobility scooter and a lightweight wheelchair.  Roy reported that he is independent with bed, chair and toilet transfers.  Roy reported that he had one fall (approximately 5-6 years ago when he fell off a stool in the kitchen).  

Roy reported he showers every other day in a shower cubicle.  Recently Roy has needed help from Jean with washing and dressing, but has been managing to do this independently for the last fortnight.  Roy reported that showering does tire him and exacerbates his shortness of breath, and he needs to sit down to rest when he gets out of the shower cubicle (there is a dining chair with arms positioned outside of the shower cubicle).  I discussed whether it may be beneficial to have something to sit on in the shower cubicle itself.  Roy initially unsure due to space, but I reassured him that I felt there was adequate space.  Roy consented to me referring him to social services.

Jean reported that she has been doing the majority of the cooking but over the past fornight Roy has been able to do more in the kitchen.  Jean reported that Roy is a very good cook and they both agreed that his best dish is his lasagne.  Roy described his appetite as excellent.  Jean does the cleaning and the laundry, and their son or daughter take her shopping.  

Roy reported that he is very independent and keen to maintain this.  He previously had a variety of jobs including being a painter and decorator and a mechanic in a hosiery factory.  He enjoys jigsaws.  He reported that it is frustrating not being able to do the things he used to be able to do.  He partly attributes this to his age, telling me that he will be 89 this year.

Roy consented to me ringing him in 2-3 weeks to review how he is getting on.  

O/ Roy sitting in rocking armchair during visit.  Observed to be able to transfer independently on/off this and mobilise in/out of the living room.  Not noticably short of breath when talking or on mobilisation.
   Home
      Aim/goal/Outcome:  Lorna Baker OT
A/ Roy has improved with regards to his breathing over the past couple of weeks.  Now less reliant on his wife Jean for support with personal care, and has started to participate in meal preparation again.  Showering and mobilising longer distances tends to exacerbate Roy's breathing.  Advice given regarding techniques/strategies to help Roy manage his breathing, and advise also given regarding energy conservation.  Would benefit from referral to social services for assessment regarding equipment for his shower cubicle (? drop down seat and grab rails).

P/ Social services referral regarding showering.
Follow up phone call in 2-3 weeks.

Management Plan:  Discharge back to the care of the GP.

Linda let me in when I arrived, asked me to lock the front door behind me 'so the man cant get in'. Linda was in lounge wear, knitting in her armchair as per previous visits. Relaxed in manner, rapport easily established. Brian was present for some of the visit.

Reports her mood is not too bad. Headaches have not been as bad and they are gradually reducing the steroid medication. Is having blood tests once a month for the next 3 months.

Linda chatted about general topics, her son likes to come round and use the games console there when they go to see Brian's sister. Linda has been knitting hats for homeless people and also Christmas decorations to help raise money for a youth hostel. 

Linda is still going out weekly to social groups with her carers. Last week she attended a new local church group, her carer could not take her so Brian dropped her off, there was a lady there she has met before so she stayed with this lady. I gave her praise for going to something new on her own. Linda stated there was a man there that she didnt know and that makes her nervous. When she see's men that she doesnt know and thye have something in their hand she will see a knife or a gun. states once she has met them a few times she feels safer and this doesnt happen.

Linda joked about her sister texting her 2000 times a day, this does stress her out, sister claiming to always be falling over or be physically unwell and Linda questions the validity of this information.

Eating and drinking ok, recent weight gain she believes is due to steroid medication. Sleep- unable to get off to sleep until 12-2am, napping during the day time. I have suggested she find ways to stay awake in the afternoons so that she is naturally tired at night time.

Continues to see 'Jonty', dissociative experience of a twin brother she believes that she has, this is a positive experience for her therefore we are not considering any further psychological or pharmalogical treatment to reduce this. No thoughts of self harm or suicide.

Linda is calmer and brighter in mood in comparison to when referred to our team earlier this year. I advised that today would be my last visit as no current role for me. In future should her mental health deteriorate GP can refer back to us.

Hello Jade,

Thank you for your enquiry regarding support for this child.
Any support for children regarding continence and/or products is initially via the Healthy Together Public Health/School Nursing Service (ScN if 5yrs old, under 5 their FHV team.)
Healthy Together (HT) provide the initial support and advice and complete the Continence Care Pathway over several months to promote toileting skills and routines and ensure there is healthy bladder and bowel function. 
This is a requirement regardless of any neurodiversity diagnosis or on-going assessments, any sensory issues and learning difficulties.
All children/parents are required to complete the pathway and parents to implement the advice consistently before a child is accepted by the Tier 2 Children's Continence Service  especially those referred for the provision of prescribed NHS continence containment products.
(There are very few exceptions  accepted without completing all the continence care pathway  those receiving end of life care and those with profound, complex medical needs/conditions  dependent on others for all aspects of the care.)
Children can be referred to The Children's Continence Service from age 4 ï¿½ years for ongoing toileting support (if showing signs of progress) or age 5 years for the provision of prescribed NHS continence containment products if the criteria are met. (Please note that pull ups are not prescribed by the Children's Continence Service).
You can make an electronic referral to the Healthy Together service via system 1 or parents can self-refer via the Healthy Together Helpline on telephone No: 0300 300 3001.
If parents are enquiring about accessing larger size /specialist products to purchase themselves please advise to access websites such as: Tena.Net, Attends, ID Expert, Depend, Abena, P&S supplies and Imedi care  where a variety of specialist products can be purchased.
Additional information can be obtained from The National Autism Society, ERIC and Bladder and Bowel UK websites.
I hope this information answers your enquiry.
Kind Regards
Hilary Kidd
